source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 2 May 1930, p. 11 ("Local elections in Ulster: nominations in Derry; rural district returns")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: BNL 2 May 1930 p11 'Limavady Rural Council', read in the block image (area 8): ten nominations, 'In a number of divisions there were no nominations, and the retiring members are deemed to be re-elected.'

note: Triennial election of Limavady rural district (23 divisions). Ten nominations were received, none contested; in the other divisions there were no nominations and the retiring members were deemed re-elected, unnamed in the report (Belfast News-Letter, 2 May 1930, p. 11). No division in Co. Londonderry was contested in 1930 (county council: Webb withdrew in Liberties), so there was no poll; the round stays filed on 1930-06-05, a provisional date not confirmed by any paper read. Five retained members recorded from reports of the new council's meetings (meetings gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
